newsitem.title: FRANCE: Thomson good for Lagardere, also Alcatel - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Thomson good for Lagardere, also Alcatel - analysts.

text.p: The French government's stated preference for Lagardere in the Thomson sale was welcomed by market analysts on Wednesday -- who also saw it as allowing Alcatel Alsthom the oportunity to get on with its recovery.

"The government has preferred industrial logic," analyst Gilbert Ferrand at CDC Bourse said on Wednesday. "This will allow the development of a defence champion which will be able to offer complete systems."
Another analyst said Alcatel would be spared a frittering away of energy and it could concentrate on telecommunications.

Analysts believe Lagardere got Thomson on very good terms. Quite apart from a symbolic one franc payment, Thomson will get a 11 billion franc recapitalisation to cut 25 billion francs of debt, of which 14 billion is owed by Thomson Multimedia.
Asset sales should bring in some 10 billion francs, including the sale of Thomson-CSF's 17 percent stake in chip-maker SGS-Thomson which could raise between 4.2-4.3 billion francs.
The sale of Thomson's 19 percent holding in Credit Lyonnais bank should bring in 2.9 billion francs.
Separately, Lagardere stands to gain 2.9 billion francs when share warrants fall due in the first half of 1997.
Alcatel shares closed up 2.43 percent at 455.7 francs. Lagardere and Thomson-CSF shares were suspended and will resume trading on Thursday.
Alcatel lost 2.22 percent on Tuesday on a rumour it had won the bidding for Thomson.
Some analysts do not rule a fall in Lagardere shares when they requote due to the dilutive effect of the deal. But on the whole there is scope for gains in the long term.
Lagardere is offering to buy out Thomson-CSF minorities at 156 francs per share, for a total 7.8 billion francs.
"The price proposed is lower than the market price but there is greater potential for gains for the new merged company," said Jacques Falzon, analyst at Transbourse.
Thomson-CSF shares have risen 47 percent since the beginning of the year. They closed on Tuesday at 161.20 francs.

The addition of Thomson-CSF will radically alter the shape of the Lagardere group, sparking speculation among some operators the company may spin off into two groups -- communications and high technology.

"With two quoted vehicles with greater business purity, there would no longer be a reason for a discount," said Falzon. He values Lagrdere at 180 francs per share while the stock closed on Tuesday at 133.10 francs.
Chairman Jean-Luc Lagardere himself raised the possibility of a spin-off at the company's last shareholders meeting, saying, "There is no plan today but why not one tomorrow?".
Meanwhile, Alcatel is free to continue acquisition talks for state-controlled nuclear power plant builder Framatome, in concert with its partner GEC Plc
